title: Context-intelligence Unit A1: baseline harness, repository fingerprint + per-file manifest contract, cache-generation layout, telemetry (D-013)
objective: Implement D-013 Unit A1 only: (a) the baseline/benchmark harness that freezes and records the EXISTING code-graph full-build behavior over a representative corpus before any behavior change; (b) the ONE reusable deterministic repository-identity + snapshot-fingerprint + per-file source-manifest service (canonical-path checkout identity per owner decision 5; HEAD + dirty-state digest + configuration versions + per-file content SHA-256 bound into the snapshot identity; canonical serialization, domain-separated hashes, explicit newline/symlink/case/Unicode/unreadable-file behavior, never silently skipping an unreadable eligible file); (c) the external cache-generation layout OUTSIDE the worktree (accepted %LOCALAPPDATA% per-checkout runtime convention) with lock + temporary generation + validation + atomic promotion and crash-safe recovery contract; (d) append-only redacted JSONL runtime telemetry outside the worktree plus a bounded committed sanitized evidence summary; (e) deterministic coverage/status fields (census accounting: eligible/indexed/excluded/failed/stale) required to prove Unit A; (f) tests and documentation including the rollback runbook. NO incremental indexing/invalidation (A2), NO context-compiler change (B), NO ontology (C), NO memory digests (D). Keep the accepted code-graph eligibility roots (owner decision 8); never modify tools/agent_supervisor/** (owner decision 9).
business_reason: D-013 owner authorization 2026-08-18: first bounded unit of the context-intelligence pipeline; baseline must be frozen before any index/context behavior changes so promotion evidence can compare honestly.
inputs: tools/code_graph/generate.py + tools/code_graph/query.py (read-only reference: existing full-build behavior, include roots, artifact conventions)
tools/agent_supervisor/durable_state.py (read-only reference: accepted canonical-path checkout identity + %LOCALAPPDATA% runtime convention; NEVER modified)
outputs: tools/repo_fingerprint.py - ONE reusable deterministic repository-identity + snapshot-fingerprint + per-file source-manifest service (versioned, domain-separated hashes)
tools/repo_index_cache.py - external cache-generation layout (outside worktree, per-checkout namespace) with lock + temp generation + validation + atomic promotion + recovery/quarantine contract
tools/repo_index_baseline.py - baseline/benchmark harness freezing existing full-build behavior over the representative corpus + redacted JSONL telemetry writer
tools/test_repo_fingerprint.py, tools/test_repo_index_cache.py, tools/test_repo_index_baseline.py - deterministic stdlib test suites
docs/CONTEXT_INTELLIGENCE_PIPELINE.md - contracts (identity, snapshot fingerprint, per-file manifest, cache generations, telemetry, coverage record fields) + rollback runbook
.github/workflows/ci.yml - ADDITIVE step(s) running the three new test modules; existing steps byte-untouched

project-control/reports/M0-T063-producer-report.md + M0-T063-baseline-evidence.md - bounded sanitized committed evidence (baseline reference digests, census accounting, no raw logs/prompts/absolute private paths)

acceptance_scenarios.name: fingerprint determinism + sensitivity
acceptance_scenarios.given: an unchanged repository snapshot (committed + uncommitted state) and fixed effective versions
acceptance_scenarios.when: the snapshot fingerprint and per-file manifest are computed twice; then a single file byte, a config digest, the parser version, and the dirty state are each changed in isolation
acceptance_scenarios.then: the two unchanged runs are byte-identical; each isolated change produces a different snapshot fingerprint; hashes are domain-separated and the manifest is canonically serialized with sorted paths and explicit encoding

acceptance_scenarios.name: census accounting is complete
acceptance_scenarios.given: the accepted code-graph eligibility roots (owner decision 8) including an unreadable eligible file and an excluded path
acceptance_scenarios.then: every eligible file is accounted as indexed or excluded/failed with a deterministic grouped reason; the unreadable file appears as a recorded failure, never a silent skip; eligible/indexed/excluded/failed/stale counts reconcile

acceptance_scenarios.name: atomic cache generation + crash recovery
acceptance_scenarios.given: a valid prior cache generation outside the worktree
acceptance_scenarios.when: a new generation write is interrupted at each crash point (before/during temp write, before validation, before promotion) and then retried; a stale lock and a concurrent writer are simulated
acceptance_scenarios.then: after every crash the prior valid generation remains loadable and the incomplete generation is detected and quarantined; the retry is idempotent; stale locks and concurrent writers are detected and handled by the explicit tested fail-closed rule; no half-index is ever observable

acceptance_scenarios.name: baseline frozen before behavior change
acceptance_scenarios.given: the representative benchmark corpus and the EXISTING unmodified code-graph generator
acceptance_scenarios.when: the baseline harness runs full builds over the frozen corpus
acceptance_scenarios.then: reference export digests + counts are recorded; runtime telemetry (append-only redacted JSONL, nullable unknown fields, never fabricated zeros) stays outside the worktree; the committed evidence summary is bounded, deterministic, and sanitized

acceptance_scenarios.name: mtime is never proof
acceptance_scenarios.given: a file whose mtime is restored after a content change
acceptance_scenarios.when: change detection runs with the mtime precheck enabled
acceptance_scenarios.then: the content-digest rule still detects the change; mtime alone never classifies a file as unchanged

risks: OVERLAP DISCLOSURE: open PR #64 (task/M0-T019-frontend-security) also touches .github/workflows/ci.yml. A1's change is one ADDITIVE step in a different region; if a real conflict with PR #64 materializes, the worker STOPS with an overlap report and proposed sequencing instead of editing (D-013 s13 hold).
Baseline must be captured from the UNMODIFIED generator before any new caching path is wired (D-013 s10/s11); the harness therefore lands and runs before any generator-facing integration in A2.
Thin client: local cache generations stay small and bounded (docs/LOW_STORAGE_CLOUD_DEVELOPMENT_POLICY.md); no citywide data, no bulk artifacts.
